description: A 110 cc air-cooled four-stroke single with a semi-automatic four-speed gearbox, the engine that moved a nation.  Simple, frugal and repairable with a screwdriver and patience.
A long padded pillion; the rear half doubles as a parcel rack.  Whole families ride on it.
A pair of long wooden oars worked standing up, facing forward, in the southern style.

//: B6 review: long-tails ran 8-13 hp engines (~10 kW), not dda's 21 kW large single.
description: A small engine bolted to a pivot on the stern, driving a propeller on the end of a long shaft.  Loud, crude and able to push a loaded boat through a weed-choked canal.
The cyclo's front bucket seat: cracked red vinyl over springs, wide enough for one passenger and a market basket, under a folding black canopy that keeps off the sun and the afternoon rain.
A deck of rough planks bolted to a steel frame and fenced with low painted rails.  Ba gác carry anything that fits and much that doesn't: refrigerators, scrap, whole households on moving day.
